answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% cut. The incumbent refuses to renegotiate and memory_c6's multi-year discount path is blocked. memory_c2 records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. I want the archived record for memory_c2 to confirm the vendor's name, the observed unit-cost delta, and whether the 'quick onboarding' still fits inside the 14-day window before the current contract lapses. If the archive confirms that the low-cost vendor can absorb primary volume without extending lead time or requiring integration work, switching primary supply is the only one of the five candidate directions that delivers the mandated cost cut without adding delivery risk. Renewing the incumbent fails the cost target. Negotiating terms fails because the incumbent has already refused to reopen price. Adding a second source would protect against shortage but does not itself cut spend and would also duplicate cost rather than reduce it. Deferring the decision is unacceptable because the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line has no buffer. The switch is still flagged for downstream-value risk: the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so any onboarding slip hits delivery immediately. That is why I verify memory_c2 before committing, and why I intend the switch only if the archived record confirms onboarding speed and cost performance consistent with what is summarized. If the archive is weaker than the summary, I fall back to renew_incumbent on short month-to-month terms to buy time, accepting that finance's target will not be met this cycle but protecting the assembly line.
